body_markdown:
Picking the right federal payroll tax return, Form 941, 944, 940, 943, or 945, isn't just paperwork trivia. It determines how often you file, what you owe, and whether the IRS considers your account compliant, and getting it wrong can turn into agency notices and penalties that a growing business really doesn't have time to unwind. This hub works through 22 of the questions employers, payroll administrators, and finance leaders ask most often about form eligibility, deposit schedules, switching rules, and edge cases, organized into five sections you can scan by decision stage.


## Form Fundamentals


Before you can pick a form, it helps to know what each one actually reports.


### What is the difference between Form 941 and Form 944?


Form 941 is the standard federal payroll tax return, filed quarterly by most employers to report withheld income tax and Social Security and Medicare taxes. Form 944 covers the same taxes but is filed once a year, and it's reserved for small employers whose total annual payroll tax liability is $1,000 or less (as of 2026), as[assigned by the IRS in writing](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-944) .


→[Form 941 quarterly filing and reconciliation questions answered](https://www.asuresoftware.com/form-941-quarterly-payroll-tax-filing-and-reconciliation-frequently-asked-questions/)


### What payroll taxes do Forms 941 and 944 cover?


Form 941 and Form 944 both cover the same three federal payroll taxes: federal income tax withheld from employee pay, the employee share of Social Security and Medicare tax, and the employer's matching share of those FICA taxes. The only difference is filing frequency. Federal unemployment tax reports separately on[Form 940](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-940) , not on either form.


→[Employer payroll tax expenses and liabilities questions answered](https://www.asuresoftware.com/employer-payroll-tax-expenses-and-liabilities-frequently-asked-questions-2/)


### What is the difference between Form 940, Form 941, and Form 944?


Form 940 reports[Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) tax](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-940) , which the employer pays alone with no employee withholding. Form 941 and Form 944 report a different set of taxes, federal income tax withholding plus employee and employer FICA, filed quarterly or annually. All three forms can apply to the same employer in the same year.


→[Filing Forms 940, 941, and 944 for growth-stage payroll operators](https://www.asuresoftware.com/how-to-file-payroll-tax-forms-940-941-and-944-for-growth-stage-payroll-operators/)


### What is the difference between Form W-2, Form 941, and Form 944?


Form W-2 reports each employee's annual wages and withheld taxes to that employee and the Social Security Administration, following the[IRS's Form W-2 requirements](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-2) . Form 941 (quarterly) or Form 944 (annually) reports the employer's aggregate payroll tax liability to the IRS instead.


## Eligibility and IRS Assignment


Form 944 eligibility isn't self-selected. Here's how the IRS decides, and how employers request or confirm assignment.


### Who files Form 944 instead of Form 941?


Employers whose total annual federal payroll tax liability is $1,000 or less (as of 2026) are eligible for Form 944, but eligibility alone isn't enough. The[IRS must notify the employer in writing](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-944) before they can switch. Because AsureCentral runs payroll, tax filing, and HR on one login against one shared data set, an employer whose assignment changes doesn't have to re-enter payroll history in a separate system to make the new form correct going forward.


### How do I know if I should file Form 941 or Form 944?


Check the notification letter the IRS mailed you. The IRS determines whether you file Form 941 or Form 944 based on your estimated annual payroll tax liability, then confirms the assignment in writing. No letter means you default to Form 941, filed quarterly. Filing the wrong one can trigger[IRS notices](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/understanding-your-irs-notice-or-letter) .


### Who determines when Form 944 should be used, the employer or the IRS?


The IRS makes the final call. Employers who expect $1,000 or less in annual payroll tax liability (as of 2026) can[request Form 944 assignment](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i944) by writing to the IRS by March 15 of the tax year, or by calling the IRS up to April 1, but the request isn't official until the IRS confirms it in writing. Clients who'd rather not track both deadlines themselves can have AsureWorks specialists submit that written request and stand ready with the April 1 phone option as a backup; AsureWorks makes that request as the client's payroll administrator, not as a co-employer, so the client stays the one on record with the IRS throughout.


### Which types of employers cannot file Form 944?


Employers with more than $1,000 in projected annual payroll tax liability (as of 2026) cannot use[Form 944](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-944) ; they must file Form 941 quarterly. Agricultural employers who pay farmworkers use[Form 943](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-943) instead of Form 944, even if their liability is low. Only employers with written IRS authorization may file Form 944.


### Is Form 944 being discontinued?


No. As of 2026,[Form 944](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-944) remains an active annual filing option for eligible small employers, and the IRS continues to issue updated versions each tax year, alongside Form 941. Employers assigned to Form 944 should always confirm they're using the current-year version posted on IRS.gov before filing.


## Filing Cadence, Deadlines, and Deposits


Once you know your form, you need the deadlines and deposit schedule that go with it.


### What is the filing deadline for Form 944?


Form 944 is due[January 31](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-944) of the year following the tax year it covers. If you deposited all payroll taxes on time and in full throughout the year, the IRS extends the deadline to February 10. Because AsureWorks specialists file on a client's behalf as their payroll administrator, not as a co-employer, they build both deadlines into that client's filing calendar and confirm which one applies based on the client's deposit record for the year.


### Is there a year-end version of Form 941?


Yes, functionally. There's no separate year-end Form 941; the fourth-quarter filing, due[January 31](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-941) , serves that role. Employers reconcile the year's four quarterly 941 filings against W-2 totals at that time to catch discrepancies before the IRS does.


→[The new Form 941, what payroll tax professionals need to be aware of](https://www.asuresoftware.com/the-new-form-941-what-payroll-tax-professionals-need-to-be-aware-of-2/)


### What is the IRS lookback period and how does it affect my deposit schedule for Form 941?


The[lookback period for Form 941 filers](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i941) is the 12-month period ending June 30 of the prior year. If your total payroll tax liability during that period was $50,000 or less (as of 2026), you deposit monthly; above $50,000, you deposit semiweekly. New employers default to monthly for their first calendar year.


### How often do you have to deposit payroll taxes when filing Form 943?


Form 943 uses the[same $50,000 monthly-versus-semiweekly deposit threshold and deposit mechanics as Form 941](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i943) : monthly depositors pay by the 15th of the following month, and semiweekly depositors pay on a Wednesday or Friday schedule tied to payday. Where Form 943 differs is the lookback period itself. Agricultural employers measure their lookback-period liability using the second preceding calendar year, not the 12-month period ending June 30 that Form 941 filers use.


## Switching Between Forms


Moving between Form 941 and Form 944 follows a specific IRS process, not employer discretion alone.


### Can I switch from Form 941 to Form 944?


Yes, but only with IRS approval, not by simply choosing a different form. If you expect $1,000 or less in annual payroll tax liability,[contact the IRS in writing by March 15 of the tax year, or by phone up to April 1](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i944) , and wait for written confirmation. AsureWorks specialists submit that request on a client's behalf and carry the account through the filing transition once the IRS confirms it in writing, without placing the client into a co-employment arrangement or changing who's on record as the employer with the IRS.


### Can I request to switch from Form 944 back to Form 941?


Yes. If your annual payroll tax liability grows above $1,000, notify the IRS and request to switch back to Form 941, in writing by March 15 of the tax year or by phone up to April 1. Once the IRS confirms the change in writing, you resume quarterly filing. AsureWorks specialists watch a client's liability trend through the year and raise a likely switch back to Form 941 before the threshold is crossed, the same way they'd flag it for any client whose payroll they run without ever becoming that client's co-employer.


### What happens if I file Form 941 when I should have filed Form 944?


Filing the wrong form can trigger IRS notices, processing delays, and potential penalties for late or incorrect filing. If you filed Form 941 but were assigned Form 944, contact the IRS to correct the record. When a misfiling like this happens, AsureWorks specialists work the correction directly with the IRS on a client's behalf, since the client remains the employer of record throughout, not Asure.


## Related Forms and Edge Cases


Form 940, 943, and 945 cover different obligations, and several edge cases trip up even experienced payroll teams.


### Do I need to file both Form 940 and Form 941?


Yes, in most cases both are required. Form 940 reports[Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) tax](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-940) , which only the employer pays. Form 941 (or Form 944, if assigned) reports withheld income tax and FICA. These are separate obligations; filing one does not satisfy the other.


### What is Form 943 and who files it?


[Form 943](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-943) is the annual federal payroll tax return for agricultural employers who pay wages to farmworkers. It covers the same federal income tax and FICA withholding as Form 941, but is filed once a year. Employers with both farm and non-farm employees may need to file both Form 943 and Form 941.


### What is Form 945 and how does it differ from Form 941?


[Form 945](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-945) reports federal income tax withheld from non-payroll payments, including pensions, annuities, gambling winnings, and backup withholding. Form 941 covers withholding from employee wages instead. A business that makes both types of payments may need to file Form 945 alongside Form 941 or Form 944.


### Can an employer with no employees file Form 944?


Generally no. An employer with no employees and no payroll tax liability for the year typically doesn't need to file Form 944, but should[confirm with the IRS](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-944) whether a final return is required. If you expect to hire again, keeping your account active may still require a return.


### Do seasonal employers need to file Form 941 every quarter?


Not necessarily. Seasonal employers who don't pay wages every quarter can check the["seasonal employer" box](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i941) on Form 941, which tells the IRS not to expect a return for quarters with no payroll. Employers must still file for any quarter in which they actually paid wages.


### How does Form 944 fit into the overall payroll tax workflow alongside Form 940 and W-2s?


Form 944 replaces Form 941 for eligible small employers, but it doesn't replace[Form 940 (FUTA)](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-940) or[W-2s](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-2) . A Form 944 filer's full annual workflow includes filing Form 944, filing Form 940, and distributing W-2s, all by January 31, and all three must reconcile to the same annual wage totals.


## Choosing the Right Form Going Forward


Picking the correct federal payroll tax return, and filing it on the correct schedule, is a compliance decision with real financial consequences for a growing employer, and it's rarely as obvious as the IRS instructions make it sound.
